title: A latent-state model links acute psychedelic treatment to sensory-guided mouse decisions
summary: A fitted generalized-linear-model hidden Markov model identified sensory-engaged and history-biased choice states in a mouse perceptual-decision task. Acute psilocybin or ketamine shifted occupancy toward sensory-engaged states while increasing response time and accuracy. First posted in September 2025 and published in Science Advances in November 2026, the work used different cohorts across analyses; the final drug comparisons included 42 psilocybin and 30 ketamine mice. State-performance relationships were checked within the study. The experiment does not establish independent replication, human therapeutic benefits or a uniquely causal interpretation of the inferred states.
ai_technology: Generalized linear model hidden Markov model (GLM-HMM) for latent decision-strategy inference

evidence.tested: The final paper reports mouse drug cohorts of 42 for psilocybin and 30 for ketamine. Repeated-measures behavioral tests show improved accuracy and longer response times at relevant doses, and GLM-HMM analyses report increased sensory-engaged state occupancy. State-specific accuracy/response-time associations provide within-study construct checks.
evidence.unknown: Inferred state-performance relationships were assessed within the study; independent validation of the state shift was not established. Sample denominators differ across versions and analyses. This acute mouse task does not establish human therapeutic benefit or a uniquely causal explanation of the latent states.
evidence.ai_role: An expectation-maximization-fitted GLM-HMM inferred latent sensory-engaged and left/right-biased states from trial-by-trial choices. State occupancy under treatment directly supports the reported strategy shift. Drift-diffusion and the separate five-fold L1 neural decoder are distinct analyses; their validation is not attributed to the GLM-HMM.

source_review.scope: Original bioRxiv v1 full Results/Methods and posted date; final primary journal full Results, Figure2 drug sample sizes and GLM-HMM Methods; preprint/final titles and affiliations. State and neural-decoder analyses distinguished.
